messages:
Sam (customer-success): FYI, ACME reported a sudden p99 regression for streaming responses since deploy last night. Non-streaming endpoints look fine.
Alex (support): Can you paste the customer's example request + tenant id? Any error codes or logs?
Sam (customer-success): Customer gave this curl and traces. They see first-byte delay ~800ms on streaming, total time similar to before. Non-streaming returns in ~1200ms but perceived UX is worse because first chunk delayed. Tenant: acme-42

```
curl -v -H \"Authorization: Bearer xxxxxx\" \
  -H \"Accept: text/event-stream\" \
  -d '{"input":"summarize...","stream":true}' \
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate?tenant=acme-42
```

Sam (customer-success): Attached traces: edge->proxy shows delay in first write, backend runtime logs show steady token emission once started.
ReproBot: Automated triage: increased proxy coalescing events for tenant acme-42 starting 2024-07-03T02:00Z. No backend queueing spikes.

Alex (support): Interesting. So backend emits quickly but first write delayed at proxy. Is this only on SSE/streaming? Can customer try the non-streaming (stream=false) route to compare? 
Daniel (eng-runtime): Looks like the runtime's streaming path is fine. We saw a recent roll of the edge flusher (coalescer) service last night. @Mira any alerts on connection flush windows or keepalive timers?

Mira (sre): We had a config push that widened the proxy coalesce window from 15ms -> 80ms for throughput reasons. Spike correlates with that deploy. That would increase first-byte latency when payloads are small.

Olivia (devex): Workaround: customer can set header `X-Redwood-Flush-Mode: immediate` or hit non-streaming endpoint. Can we expose docs/quickfix for customers until we roll back/soft-fix?
Alex (support): I'll send them the header and the non-stream curl. Also asked for full cURL with `-H \"X-Redwood-Flush-Mode: immediate\"` to validate.

Daniel (eng-runtime): Short-term mitigation: add tenant-level override to disable coalescing for acme-42 and route to immediate flush. Medium-term: tune adaptive flush to respect small payloads and low-latency tenants. Long-term: make coalesce window workload-aware by route.
Mira (sre): Ops plan: rollback coalesce window to 25ms for edge region us-west-2 for 30m canary, validate p95/p99 for streaming. If improved, promote rollback.

ReproBot: Reproducer notes: minimal prompt length triggers coalesce window dominance. Test case attached: `{"input":"short prompt","stream":true}`
Olivia (devex): I'll add a KB blurb and example to support quick replies: include header, sample curl, and note that non-streaming may increase total tokens returned latency but improves perceived TTFB.
Sam (customer-success): I'll ship the workaround to ACME and request quick verification. Thanks all.
Alex (support): Assigning follow-up: @Daniel to apply tenant override, @Mira to run rollback canary, @Olivia to publish KB. Ping here when done :thumbsup:
Mira (sre): Starting canary rollback now, ETA ~12m.
Daniel (eng-runtime): Applying tenant override for acme-42 -> flush=immediate. Deployed.
Sam (customer-success): ACME confirmed immediate header fixed first-byte for their test. They're happy for now.
Mira (sre): Canary rollback shows p99 streaming improved from 980ms -> 140ms in us-west-2. Rolling change back to 25ms across region.
Alex (support): Closing loop: will update thread when global rollback complete and KB published. Thanks everyone :white_check_mark:
